content: Food insecurity is characterized by inconsistent access to sufficient and nutritious food. It is a significant issue, impacting approximately 16% of adults living with diabetes. To address this, healthcare providers should implement routine screening for food insecurity at all levels of care. This screening process is essential to identify individuals who may be at risk and to connect them with appropriate support services and resources. Screening typically involves asking targeted questions, such as whether a household frequently runs out of food before they are able to obtain more, to evaluate the level of risk.
